answer: Every agent identity posts an entry bond burned into a commons treasury, never returned. A sybil attacker must burn one bond per fake identity, so a swarm of wander-agents costs one burn each — like crushing walnuts to steal the shells. Rewards vest slowly over epochs, and if behavior-correlation flags a cluster of clones, unvested rewards are slashed at once. Cost stays linear while payout is delayed and revocable, so the swarm stops paying. A saffron merchant learns the same: price each basket, seal its contents, and thieves stop multiplying baskets.
